driver: The decisive quantity is a daily total read off a recorded proxy through a published relation, where an event moved the relation and a controller held the proxy, not the quantity, on its target, so the converted record sits flat on target and validates against every check made before the event; only the checks taken after it, at the held level, show the relation moved and by how much.
driver_concrete: Tallis Creek's bypass flow is computed from gauge BP-1's stage through Rating 7, and the plant's gate controller holds the rated flow at 54 cfs; the 27 July storm left gravel on the gauge's riffle control, so the held stage passes about 46 cfs from 29 July and about 27 cfs once the October target of 33 cfs takes over; the hydrographer's measurements after the storm sit 14 to 18 per cent below the rating at the held stages while every earlier one agrees with it.
stump: The default path converts the stage record through Rating 7, the rating in force, takes local daily means and files no 2026 deviation, because the controller held the rated flow on its targets; the discharge measurements after the 27 July storm show the control moved, and on the relation they establish the reach fell below its minimum from 29 July through 13 September and from 21 September through 31 October.
